checks: Every positive fiber has bounded projection density along u from the containing compact section bound and the factor 1/|u|. Translating by an arbitrary base tilt keeps that bound; the infimum over tilts therefore preserves the common Lipschitz estimate and monotonicity.

For sufficiently negative s the fully captured bases contain a closed halfspace trace containing j. Perturb a finite minimizing marginal trace outward to put j strictly inside and retain its trace, then normalize the threshold to -1. The scaled tilt -s a0 gives exactly that trace when -s exceeds the finite support bound divided by the strict gap. The right plateau follows from the zero tilt.

The resulting continuous survival function has compact support and total mass D_j. Continuity provides a quantile even at t=D_j and when the tail has flat intervals; the threshold exchange inequality and layer-cake identity give the full infimum formula without differentiating a quantile.

The balanced row capacity is at least D_j, and constant densities on each positive fiber realize any scaled feasible row. Strict separation at an epsilon-raised support point gives positive coefficient on the moment; the hinge dual bound and reverse weak duality are valid even at a boundary mass. Comparing the fixed-tilt tail to its pointwise infimum inside the integral gives the stated inequality.
